placement of total responsibility on the respective bureau head is tantamount to localizing implementation of Executive Order 11644, which is contrary to the spirit of that order. There must be some type of scientific criteria established by the Department of the Interior which would influence and aid the respective bureau heads in implementation of the order.
Basically, throughout the draft, the tone is negative and discriminatory toward off-road vehicle users. There is continual restatement of the position that trails may be established only if the bureau head determines that off-road vehicle use will not adversely affect the natural, aesthetic or scenic values. The draft fails to emphasize the responsibility of the bureau head to indeed determine these facts. To the contrary, he may comply with the standards established in the draft simply by making no determination whatsoever, stating that adverse effects are likely in his judgement.
Again, I believe this possibility indicates the need for a definite set of scientific guidelines for the individual bureau heads to follow.
Your department, of course, is aware of this need, since it was expressed early in the Task Force Study on Off-Road Recreational Vehicles. On page 68 of that study is the paragraph, "The Task Force believes that essentially what is necessary to plan adequately for outdoor recreation and ORRV use is a land classification system specifically designed to protect the resources, provide safe and sane recreation and allow for as rational and balanced, yet diversified, an outdoor recreation program as possible providing a place for the motorized vehicle user on public lands within this framework should be possible without lowering other outdoor recreation standards."
This statement by the Task Force reflects very accurately the feeling of the American Motorcycle Association, and of the AMA-Motorcycle Industry Council Combined Committee on Land Use. This committee, composed of delegates from the AMA and the MIC, presently is reviewing resumes by professional ecologists. The group has resolved to hire one of these gentlemen for the purpose of establishing guidelines in a very comprehensive and clear textbook fashion. Through such a set of guidelines we hope to establish fair and equitable use of the land, knowing full well that some public land will be lost to the use of off-road recreational vehicles, yet with the feeling that our effort to cooperate will be returned by those with other interests.
Since the AMA and the MIC already have begun work towards such a set of guidelines, perhaps the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation or the Department of the Interior would be interested in working with us on such a study. I am sure that you will agree that such a study is necessary for proper implementation of Executive Order 11644.
